newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia central bank vows to push down peso.
newsitem.headline: Colombia central bank vows to push down peso.

text.p: Colombia's central bank promised stronger intervention in currency markets to push down the value of the peso next year, its co-director Hernando Jose Gomez said Friday.
He warned that without active intervention an expected flood of dollars into the country from increased exports of crude oil would drive up the Colombian currency.

The central bank has come under fire from leading exporters and government ministers in recent weeks as the peso continues to strengthen, thereby slashing value of export earnings when converted into the Colombian currency.

"There will be more active intervention in the money markets by the central bank next year. The exact level will depend on the inflation target for 1997 that we're currently studying," Gomez told the second day of the annual conference of Colombia's National Exporters' Association.
Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said on Thursday he hoped the peso would drop to a more beneficial exchange rate next year but mentioned no precise goal.
The 1996 target was for a 13.5 percent devaluation of the peso against the dollar.
